summary.headline: POWERGRID delivered ₹28,206 crore capitalisation and ~₹40,000 crore capex in FY26, guiding FY27 capex to ₹37,000 crore and capitalisation to ₹30,000 crore.
summary.overview: Management said FY26 capex (close to ₹40,000 crore against an initial ₹28,000 crore guide) and capitalisation (₹28,206 crore against a ₹25,000 crore commitment) both beat guidance. Standalone PAT rose 4% to about ₹15,921 crore and consolidated PAT rose 3% to about ₹15,928 crore, with total income of ₹47,684 crore versus ₹47,459 crore. Management flagged a natural RTM revenue decline as assets reach 12 years, offset by FY26 capitalisation that it expects to flow into FY27 revenue. The pipeline was described as ₹1.7 lakh crore of works in hand and ₹1.1 lakh crore under bidding, with new avenues in BESS, integrated storage under Section 62, and the first international PPP in Kenya.

segments.name: TBCB (tariff-based competitive bidding)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 81% of the ₹1.7 lakh crore works in hand (₹1.37 lakh crore). Management said FY26 saw 9 TBCB wins out of 28 projects floated, at a total tariff of about 44% share.

segments.name: RTM (regulated tariff mechanism)
segments.commentary: Works in hand of about ₹28,000 crore. Revenue is on a natural downward trajectory after assets complete 12 years, offset in FY26 by ~₹1,700 crore of depreciation-related gaps covered by other income items.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹1,195 crore; first 400G interface in India, first international long-distance link to Bhutan, and a 1,000-rack data centre at Manesar expected to be visible in the next quarter.

segments.name: Consultancy
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹1,755 crore versus ₹799 crore in FY25, with 39 domestic orders and 62 ongoing projects, and 8 international orders across 25 countries.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex initial guidance of about ₹37,000 crore; FY28 capex expected above ₹40,000 crore, with management indicating a ₹40,000-45,000 crore range.
FY27 capitalisation guidance of up to ₹30,000 crore initially; FY28 capitalisation expected to move to about ₹35,000 crore.
FY27 expected to show full revenue benefit of FY26 capitalisation, which came mainly in the later part of FY26.
Management said FY27-FY28 earnings growth is likely to be better than the last three years when asked directly; it did not quantify this.
Integrated storage (BESS) capacity target not yet given; management said numbers would follow once Section 62 regulatory clarity emerges.
Pang-Kaithal HVDC project excluded from the ₹1.7 lakh crore works in hand pending Government of India review.
capex_capacity: Capitalisation of 4,765 ckm of transmission lines and 72,055 MVA of substation capacity added in FY26; 9 new substations taking the total to 291, and total transmission lines at 1.84 lakh ckm and 624 GVA transformation capacity at 31 March 2026.

Transformer and reactor manufacturing capacity in India is about 300 GVA against demand of 400+ GVA a year; the company is moving to bulk procurement and project timelines were extended to 26-30+ months from 18 months.
Gross fixed assets crossed ₹3 lakh crore; 11 HVDC projects are running with about 101 GW of the 120 GW inter-regional capacity.
New substations commissioned include Bhadla, Ramgarh/Dausa (8 months from foundation), Bikaner-3, KPS-2, KPS-3, Narela and Ananthapuram.
Pilot 1,000-rack data centre at Manesar expected to be visible within the next quarter; 220 kV mobile GIS in place, with 132 kV and 400 kV mobile GIS expected within this calendar year.
demand_pricing: Works in hand ₹1.7 lakh crore (TBCB ₹1.37 lakh crore, RTM ₹28,000 crore, others ₹4,200 crore), excluding Pang-Kaithal HVDC.

Under-bidding pipeline of ₹1.1 lakh crore, including ₹5,270 crore of intra-State; major projects include Barmer Phase 4, Vizag Green Hydrogen, Jam Khambhaliya, Krishnagiri, Lakadia, ERWR and Nawada-Durgapur.
Management cited a ₹7.9 lakh crore opportunity under the 900+ GW by 2036 anchor programme and ₹6.4 lakh crore from Brahmaputra basin hydro; 22 HVDC schemes (127 GW) are in planning or bidding.
Intra-State TBCB thresholds are ₹150-250 crore by state; the smallest project POWERGRID has bid was about ₹60 crore.
Management said electricity share in the energy basket is about 22% and is expected to rise, supporting transmission demand.

On competition, management said it bids on risk-return framework and declined to quantify changes in TBCB tariff or IRR; equity IRR guidance of 11-13% was described as possibly better, with change-in-law as a cost pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the Q4 FY26 EBITDA decline and whether new TBCB projects use service concession accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the natural RTM tariff dip after 12 years of asset life; new BOOT-method TBCB projects are accounted for using the financial lease model.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and commissioning expectations for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex initial guidance of about ₹37,000 crore; FY28 expected beyond ₹40,000 crore, in a ₹40,000-45,000 crore range. Capitalisation guided at ₹30,000 crore for FY27 and about ₹35,000 crore for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block versus NCT cost variance on projects and inflation indicators?
qa_highlights.answer: No project-level variance was given; management said costs are factored into bids and surprises such as force majeure and change in law are addressed under the Transmission Service Agreement.

qa_highlights.question: Market share and whether competitive intensity in TBCB is rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has bid TBCB for about 14 years and selects projects by risk-return framework rather than volume; it did not indicate a change in intensity.

qa_highlights.question: Equity IRR on TBCB projects given cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns could be better than the 11-13% range, as cost-plus RTM rewards cost but TBCB rewards efficiency, and change-in-law provisions protect against surprises.

qa_highlights.question: Phasing of capex and capitalisation in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing depends on individual project completions, expects an even spread across quarters, and noted that the Q4-heavy FY26 was incidental.

qa_highlights.question: Regulated equity on standalone and consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulated equity exists only in standalone; TBCB projects have no regulated equity.

risks_watch: Revenue dip as RTM assets reach 12 years of life, with management noting FY26 ~₹1,700 crore gap covered by other items; FY27 revenue depends on capitalisation flow-through.
Equipment supply constraints: transformer and reactor capacity of ~300 GVA against 400+ GVA demand; project delays from procurement and labour shortages.
Right-of-way and compensation: market-rate determination via three valuers introduced; resolution timelines unclear.
Cost inflation on TBCB projects where bids may not fully reflect rising conductor, transformer, land and interest costs; reliance on change-in-law recovery.
Intra-State payment security and right-of-way risk versus ISTS; PRAAPTI portal extension to intra-State is pending.
Monitor SPV consolidation (28 SPVs in process) and the timing of the ₹1.1 lakh crore bidding pipeline, which management said could slip by a couple of months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and capitalisation beats, with repeated emphasis on past guidance being exceeded. Cautious and deferential on timing questions (HVDC, bidding, BESS targets, IRRs), repeatedly redirecting them to the planner or saying numbers would come later, and some answers on intra-State risk and cost pass-through were general rather than quantified.
key_quotes: The capitalization guidance stands exceeded. The system availability stands exceeded.
So, this current financial year i.e., FY26-27 would be witnessing the complete fruits of that particular capitalization.
Transmission is the only way how electricity can move.
